title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #1
body: She started in QA because everyone starts in QA, and she will defend QA with a fire you were not prepared for. Ask how she got in. Code Academy, DEA, Step, or a bootcamp her cousin recommended, then six months of applying, then a junior role at a bank. If she says "manual" she's one year in. If she says "automation" she's three years in and already talking to a company in Warsaw. It's a sealed deal if her parents still describe her job to relatives as "bankda işləyir."
caption:
Tip #1 😭 Baku IT girls, this is not an attack, it's a documentary.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #2
body: Check the coffee. Not whether she drinks it, where. A laptop at Coffee Moffie on a Saturday is not leisure, that is a second job or a course. Ask what the course is. Google certificates, a UX bootcamp, IELTS, or Polish lessons, and each one is a different exit plan. If it's IELTS she's leaving within eighteen months. If it's Polish she's already accepted. It's a sealed deal if the laptop has a sticker from a conference she went to alone.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #3
body: Listen for the two conversations she's having simultaneously. One is about promotion, product, and stack. The other is her mother, every week, asking a question that is never actually about work. She is 26. The company wants her in Warsaw. Her mother wants her in Baku. Nobody is wrong and everyone is tired. If she changes the subject when you ask about family, don't push. It's a sealed deal when she describes the job offer and the wedding invitation in the same sentence, in the same tone.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #4
body: Watch the office wardrobe. Zara and Mango from Ganjlik or 28 Mall, worn like a uniform, nothing that photographs as trying. The IT girls dress down and the marketing girls dress up, and both know exactly what the other is doing. Check the bag for a laptop that is too heavy and a charger she has lost three times. Ask about the team lunch. There is always a team lunch, it is always the same four women, and they have a group chat older than most marriages. It's a sealed deal if she's the one who books the table.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #5
body: Ask what her salary is in and watch the pause. Everyone in Baku IT knows the number and nobody says it. Manat means a local bank. Dollars means outsourcing to Europe. If she freelances on the side, she does not mention it, ever, because the last person who did got a lecture from a relative about tax. Check for a Payoneer card in the wallet. It's a sealed deal if she has a spreadsheet tracking the manat rate that she updates by hand.

Tip #5 😭 Baku IT girls, this is not an attack, it's a documentary.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #6
body: Look at what she does with the annual leave. Not Antalya, everyone does Antalya. Georgia for a weekend, Istanbul for the shopping, Dubai if it was a good year, and one trip somewhere alone that she posted almost nothing from. That last one is the tell. She went with two friends from the office, and the photos are on a private highlight with a name that means nothing to anyone else. It's a sealed deal if her passport has more stamps than her mother knows about.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku IT Girl. Tip #7
body: Ask her about HR. Every IT girl in Baku either is an HR, dated an HR, or was interviewed by an HR who asked whether she was planning to get married soon. That question gets asked constantly and it is illegal and it happens anyway, in a nice office, in a nice voice. She has an answer ready. She has had it ready for years. It's a sealed deal if she can quote the question back to you word for word, in the exact tone it was asked.
